newsitem.title: USA: N.J. police find anti-abortion flyers in cereal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. police find anti-abortion flyers in cereal.

text.p: Flyers with graphic illustrations of abortions have been found stuffed into breakfast cereal boxes and other packages in several New Jersey supermarkets, police said Friday.

"This is the work of sick individuals who have made an effort to deliver their anti-abortion message in a most bizarre and illegal manner," said Joseph Delaney, police director of Ramsey, a New York City suburb.

Delaney said the seals on the cereal boxtops were broken and carefully closed after the pamphlets were inserted. One page of the two-page flyer urged people to pray to Jesus and the other included five illustrations of a procedure condemned as "partial-birth abortion" by anti-abortion activists.
The flyers started appearing before Thanksgiving, when a 7-year-old Ramsey, N.J., boy opened a cereal box at home and found the pamphlet, police said.

The products tampered with include cereals, toothpaste, toilet paper and one of the local newspapers. The flyers have been found at at least six supermarkets and in several towns, including Allendale, Paramus, Hillsdale and Fair Lawn.

Delaney said if a seal is broken, the crime is product tampering. If the flyers are placed inside the boxes without the seal being broken, the violation is fourth-degree harassment. Both can result in 18 months in jail and a $1,000 fine.
